newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. orders total withdrawal from east Zaire city.
newsitem.headline: U.N. orders total withdrawal from east Zaire city.

text.p: The United Nations will send planes to the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu on Saturday to evacuate some 100 U.N. and other aid workers due to worsening security, officials said.
Ethnic Tutsi rebels have been fighting Zairean troops in the area for more than a week.

"All Bukavu office staff and all expatriate aid personnel are to be relocated. We have received authorisation for three flights from Bukavu to Uganda today," said Paul Stromberg, a spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
"Plans are being drawn up for the total of 98 expatriates, U.N. and NGO (Non-Governmental Organisation), to be taken out including 16 UNHCR staff," he added by telephone from Kigali.
"The aid community will be escorted by a contingent of Zairean guards to Bukavu airport," he added. Other aid officials said perhaps as many as 108 aid workers would be evacuated.
They said two Buffalo aircraft were being sent from Entebbe airport in Uganda to Bukavu. Each plane takes 42 passengers.
The decision to pull out all foreign aid staff followed an order by the U.N. security office in New York for a total or partial withdrawal from Bukavu because of increasing insecurity.
